title: Long O Teams
kidRule: When two letters team up to say long O, OA usually goes in the middle of a word and OW goes at the end. Watch out: OW can also say 'ow!' as in cow.
hint: Listen for the long O. Is it in the middle of the word or right at the end? That tells you which team to pick.
reminder: Long O is spelled O-A in the middle of a word and O-W at the end.

check.question: Why does ELBOW end with OW and not OA?
check.correctAnswer: Long O at the end of a word is usually spelled OW!
distractors: Because OA is only used in words about water
Because W always comes after the letter O

words.def: The front part of your neck, and the tube inside it that food goes down.
words.sent: Warm soup felt good on my sore throat.
words.story: Many male frogs puff up their throat like a balloon to make their calls louder!
words.card: The frog puffed up its *throat* *at* the moon and sang opera!

words.def: The bendy joint in the middle of your arm.
words.sent: I bumped my elbow on the table.
words.story: Your 'funny bone' is not a bone at all. It is a nerve that runs past your elbow, which is why a bump there tingles!
words.card: I tied a *bow* on my *elbow* so it would look fancy for dinner!

words.def: A dark shape made when something blocks the light.
words.sent: My shadow followed me down the sidewalk.
words.story: Your shadow is longest early in the morning and late in the afternoon, and shortest in the middle of the day!
words.card: My *shadow* *had* a nap while I did all the running!

words.def: To use something that belongs to someone else and then give it back.
words.sent: May I borrow your purple marker?
words.story: Some libraries let you borrow more than books. You can check out toys, tools and even telescopes!
words.card: Can I *borrow* your boat to *row* across this giant bowl of soup?

words.def: Resting on top of the water without sinking.
words.sent: The little raft stayed afloat all the way down the river.
words.story: Sea otters hold paws while they sleep, so they stay afloat together and do not drift apart!
words.card: One brave *oat* stayed *afloat* in my cereal bowl all morning!

words.def: To move closer to someone or something.
words.sent: The deer ran off when we tried to approach it.
words.story: Pilots have a special name for the last part of a flight, when the plane lines up with the runway. They call it the approach!
words.card: My *app* beeps whenever sneaky squirrels *approach* the cookie jar!

words.sent: We leave for the beach tomorrow morning.
words.story: Because the Earth has time zones, when it is Monday evening in New York it is already Tuesday morning in Tokyo. It is already tomorrow there!
words.card: *Tom* says that *tomorrow* he will teach his turtle to tap dance!

words.def: Black, crumbly burned wood used for cooking on a grill or for drawing.
words.sent: The artist drew a horse with a stick of charcoal.
words.story: Some cave paintings drawn with charcoal are more than 30,000 years old!
words.card: The snowman traded his *coal* buttons for *charcoal* so he could draw himself a mustache!

words.def: A flat brown bug that runs very fast and likes dark places.
words.sent: A cockroach scurried under the fridge.
words.story: Cockroaches are older than the dinosaurs! Their ancient relatives were scurrying around about 300 million years ago.
words.card: A *roach* is just a *cockroach* who is too shy to say his whole name!

words.def: A soft, puffy white candy that is yummy when toasted.
words.sent: I toasted a marshmallow over the campfire.
words.story: Marshmallows were first made from the sap of a plant called the marsh mallow, which grows in wet, marshy places!
words.card: Is it against the rules to *allow* a *marshmallow* to nap in my hot cocoa?
